 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Stan Wawrinka is back on the ATP Tour this week after receiving a wildcard for the Lyon Open. 
 The ATP 250 tournament is now underway in France, where Wawrinka will play for the penultimate time in his glittering career. Wawrinka will retire in Basel later this month, hanging up his racket on home soil at the ATP 500 event.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But first he takes on the Lyon Open, where the draw has certainly not been kind to the 41-year-old. It would be an astonishing feat should Wawrinka go all the way this week, although he does, of course, have absolutely nothing to prove on the court at this stage.
 Stan Wawrinka handed brutal Lyon Open draw
 Wawrinka is in the top half of the Lyon Open draw, with the veteran starting out in the first round against Spanish youngster Martin Landaluce. Should he emerge victorious, the veteran then has the hardest match on paper against top seed Flavio Cobolli. The Italian, who was runner-up at this year's French Open, has a bye into round two.
 The quarterfinals don't exactly get much easier for Wawrinka, who could face either fifth seed Brandon Nakashima or fellow icon Matteo Berrettini should he make it that far. After that, Lorenzo Musetti and Valentin Vacherot represent possible semifinal opponents.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement And should Wawrinka enjoy a stunning run all the way to the final in Lyon, he could be awaited by Taylor Fritz. Fritz is a wildcard in Lyon too, with the American ace doing what he can to secure qualification for the ATP Finals next month.
 It's certainly far from easy for Wawrinka, but he can rest in the knowledge that the Lyon crowd will be backing him all the way. His superb career speaks for itself, and fans will likely turn up to see the Swiss legend in action before he calls time on his playing days.
 The tournament is one of three ATP 250 events running concurrently in the calendar following the conclusion of the Shanghai Masters. The likes of Daniil Medvedev and Stefanos Tsitsipas headline the entry list in Almaty, while Arthur Fils and Jiri Lehecka are among those playing in Brussels. The latter event has, however, already been seriously impacted by injuries, with Felix Auger-Aliassime and Holger Rune having both withdrawn from the tournament in Belgium.
